newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine call rate falls as peso demand eases.
newsitem.headline: Philippine call rate falls as peso demand eases.

text.p: The Philippine interbank call loan rate fell to an average of 11.59375 percent as banks had squared their position by unloading their Treasury bills and dollars holdings earlier in the week, traders said.

"Many banks thought that the tightness in the market would extend for the rest of the week. They have unloaded their government securities and sold their dollars to cover their reserve deficiencies," one trader said.
The interbank rate rose to 12.59375 percent on Wednesday.
Turnover in the market was moderate with 20.378 billion pesos changing hands among 35 lenders and 22 borrowers.
Another trader said that the tightness early in the week was because some banks were preparing for the maiden issue of the 10-year T-bonds which was offered on Tuesday.

More than 9.9 billion pesos worth of tenders were received, but the auction committee accepted only 2.0 billion pesos worth. With the excess funds floating in the market, traders were locking up their money back in T-bills.
Three-month bills were being bought even if its effective yields were at 11.2 to 11.3 percent, lower than the auction's average of 11.5 percent.
Six-month bills were being bought at 11.6 percent, while the one-year bills at 12.6 percent.
